document.title: Security audit 2026-11-07 (13): Linux and macOS verification script

acknowledgments.summary: audit of pull request test/verify-linux-macos before merge, directed by the maintainer

notes.title: Summary
notes.text: Audit of verify-linux-macos.py, the Python port of verify-windows.ps1 for Linux (native and Flatpak OBS) and macOS, its CI checks, and a cleanup fix in verify-windows.ps1. No vulnerabilities found. The residual risks from NIXIE-SEC-2026-11-07-5 apply with one improvement noted below.

notes.title: What the script changes on the tester's machine
notes.text: Same as the Windows script: the obs-websocket config.json under the OBS config folder (~/.config/obs-studio, the Flatpak folder under ~/.var/app, or ~/Library/Application Support/obs-studio) is read as bytes first and restored exactly, or removed if it did not exist; a temporary scene collection is created through obs-websocket and only new files in the scenes folder whose names start with NixieVerify are deleted; the report goes to a new folder on the Desktop or in the home folder. No root or sudo is used.

notes.title: Code review
notes.text: WebSocket: a minimal RFC 6455 client to 127.0.0.1 only, masking every frame as the RFC requires, checking the Sec-WebSocket-Accept reply, and bounding reads by the frame length; authentication uses the obs-websocket SHA-256 challenge. One-time port from the OS and a 24-character password from the secrets module. Retries only on status 207 (NotReady), with a 120-second limit. PNG decoding handles only 8-bit RGB/RGBA non-interlaced images from OBS and rejects anything else; all indexes are bounded by the decoded image size. External commands are run with argument lists, never a shell: pgrep/pkill with the fixed process name (the script refuses to run while OBS is already open, so only the OBS it started is signalled), xdg-open/open with the report URL, gdbus/xdg-open/open -R with the report image path, wl-copy/xclip/pbcopy/osascript for the clipboard, zenity/kdialog/osascript/tkinter for the question box, notify-send for notifications. Text passed into AppleScript is escaped (backslashes and quotes); the only values are fixed messages and the tester's own report path. The report URL is built with urllib.parse.urlencode. The submission works as reviewed in log 6: nothing is sent by the script.

notes.title: Residual risk 1 improved
notes.text: On Linux and macOS the script handles SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP (sent when the terminal window is closed) by running its cleanup, so closing the terminal mid-run now restores the WebSocket settings. Only SIGKILL or a power loss can leave the WebSocket server enabled with the unknown random password.

notes.title: Fixes found while testing (not security)
notes.text: OBS removes punctuation from scene collection file names, so the cleanup pattern NixieVerify-<date>-<time> never matched and both scripts left the temporary collection behind. Fixed in both scripts. Also fixed in the new script before merge: OBS on Linux ignores SIGTERM in some versions, so it is closed with SIGINT; and the script now reaps its own OBS process before checking whether OBS is still running.

notes.title: Test evidence
notes.text: Three full runs on Debian 13 with OBS 30.2.3 (Wayland, GNOME) against a separate OBS config folder: all 22 automated checks passed; the final run showed a clean OBS shutdown, a normal WebSocket close (code 1000), the temporary collection removed and the WebSocket config restored. macOS has been checked in CI without OBS only.

notes.title: Result
notes.text: No findings. Logged as required by the project's audit policy.
